question.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
question.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the second row of ${I}_{3}$ by $-\frac{1}{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary 
row operation ${R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}$ to $A.$
